newsitem.title: UK: N.Ireland outperforms other British regions - survey.
newsitem.headline: N.Ireland outperforms other British regions - survey.

text.p: The Northern Ireland economy continues to outperform other regions in Britain despite the collapse of the IRA ceasefire last February and a summer of street disorder, a survey published on Monday showed.

But the survey, carried out by Coopers & Lybrand, said it was clear that the extent of medium-term investment in Northern Ireland would be influenced by the political situation there and fears of violence.

"The Northern Ireland economy is quite healthy and it remains amongst the UK's top performing regions with both investment and exports continuing to rise," Stephen Kingon, Northern Ireland managing partner at Coopers & Lybrand said.
"However, despite these strong short-term indicators, the business community is clearly worried about the current political situation and cutbacks in government spending."
Evidence of reduced public spending in Northern Ireland, where the public sector accounts for about 60 percent of GDP, is causing concern, the survey said.
Kingon said that if these issues remained major concerns, investment intentions could be deferred, impacting on the economy.
The survey also said that BSE remained a serious concern in Northern Ireland with farmers, processors and ancillary services severely affected.

But generally business in Northern Ireland continued to perform well with both order books and profits continuing to rise although economic growth was not as strong as in 1995, mainly because of concern about the political situation.
